facts.text: Kalona sprang to life when the Burlington, Cedar Rapids and Northern Railway opened a 66‑mile branch through the town in 1879.
Amish settlers arrived in the 1840s, making Kalona one of Iowa’s earliest European communities.
Kalona’s New Order Amish community is among the most technology‑friendly, even allowing tractors for field work.
The Kalona Historical Village, opened in 1969 after moving the original train depot, preserves 12 historic buildings and four museums.
Inside the village, the Mennonite Museum showcases Amish and Mennonite heritage through immersive exhibits and streetscape recreations.
Kalona houses the Iowa Mennonite Archives, a research center located within the Kalona Historical Village.
